title: tenant-crypto-tag-propagation-and-rbac-v2-policy-matrix
author: Anika Bose
description: Motivation: ensure cryptographic provenance and tenant attributes flow end-to-end for auditability and access control. This PR implements immutable crypto-tag propagation in request headers and audit records, exposes those tags as first-class attributes in the RBAC v2 evaluation pipeline, and ships a small policy-matrix generator to help security teams validate tenant scoping policies. Summary: 1) carry X-Redwood-Crypto-Tag through the API gateway, internal RPCs, and eventual audit forwarder without allowing mutation by downstream services; 2) enrich audit events with crypto_tag and signer_fingerprint fields and persist them to the audit index; 3) add crypto_tag and tenant_attribute predicates to the RBAC v2 engine and wire them into policy evaluation; 4) include a tool (scripts/policy-matrix-generator) that expands high-level policy rules into a matrix with example tenants and crypto tags for reviewers; 5) provide a migration/rollout path behind feature flag security.crypto_tag.enabled. Implementation notes: header validation happens at the JWT introspection layer (authn) and at the gateway ingress. The header is canonicalized to a hashed form to avoid PII leakage and is signed with the platform key before being forwarded to internal services. The rbac evaluator receives an attributes bag that includes crypto_tag and tenant_attrs which can be referenced from policy expressions. The audit forwarder now appends crypto provenance fields and exposes an opt-in index mapping in the private deployment installer. Migration and rollout: feature flag default is off; rollout plan is staged: enable in dev -> enable in staging for all tenants -> opt-in for enterprise customers -> globally on after 2 weeks and metric stability checks. Backwards compatibility: services that don't understand the new attributes will safely ignore them; audit indices will be populated only when the feature flag is enabled for a control group. Testing: unit tests for header parsing and policy predicates, integration tests covering gateway->service->audit path, and end-to-end smoke with a sample tenant. Docs and ops: added runbook entry, upgrade notes for private installer, and sample policies. Checklist: [x] header propagation and signing implemented [x] rbac attribute plumbing implemented [x] audit enrichment implemented [x] policy-matrix generator added [x] unit/integration tests added [x] docs and upgrade notes added

review_comments: Marco Diaz: The header signing step looks good; please add a TTL check on the signed token to avoid replay across long-lived connections.
Anika Bose: Added TTL check to the signer and included a unit test to assert replay rejection for stale tags.

Priya Nair: We need stronger guarantees that downstream services cannot overwrite the canonical crypto tag. Suggest rejecting requests with X-Redwood-Crypto-Tag when the service writes a different tag to downstream calls.

Anika Bose: Implemented gateway-level mutation protection and added a lint rule to fail builds if services attempt to set the header in outbound clients. Documented expected behavior in the migration notes.
Lucas Park: Integration tests are failing intermittently in CI due to timing in the signer; can we make the signer deterministic in tests or mock the clock?
Anika Bose: Tests updated to use a deterministic test clock; CI rerun passes.
Security review (internal): Please confirm hashed form meets PCI/PHI controls; add KMS key rotation guidance to docs.
Anika Bose: Added section on KMS rotation and key policy recommendations to docs/security/crypto_tagging.md

release_notes: Introduces immutable crypto-tag propagation header (X-Redwood-Crypto-Tag) to improve audit provenance.
Exposes crypto_tag and tenant_attribute predicates in RBAC v2 so policies can reference cryptographic provenance and tenant metadata.
Adds audit enrichment for crypto provenance fields; private installer includes optional index mappings for search/alerts.
Feature gated behind security.crypto_tag.enabled; rollout recommended via staged enablement and metric monitoring.
